# Braddock Concrete

> Concrete & excavation contractor on Utah's Wasatch Front — flatwork,
> footings & foundations, retaining walls, site prep, digs, trenching, and
> grading. One crew, one contract, bids in writing.

## About

Braddock Concrete handles the two trades every project starts with — the dig
and the pour — with one crew on one schedule. Base is compacted in lifts,
mixes are air-entrained for Utah freeze-thaw, joints are saw-cut on time, and
the bid you sign is the bid you pay. A Spravek company, alongside Alpine Fence
& Deck, SPX Construction, Harlow Landscapes, and Relentless Equipment.

- Region: Utah — Wasatch Front (based in Utah County)
- Cities served: Lehi, Salt Lake City, Sandy, Draper, Alpine, Highland,
  Pleasant Grove, Provo, Saratoga Springs, Eagle Mountain, American Fork,
  Orem, Herriman, Riverton, Bluffdale
- Counties served: Salt Lake, Utah, Summit, Davis, Wasatch
- Price tier: residential / light commercial ($$)

## Concrete Flatwork

- Driveways & extensions
- Patios, walkways & steps
- Garage & shop slabs
- RV pads & approaches
- Stamped & broom finishes
- Curb, gutter & aprons

## Foundations & Structural

- Footings & foundation walls
- Garage & shop foundations
- Grade beams, piers & pads
- Retaining walls
- Window wells & egress
- Tear-out & replacement

## Excavation & Dirt Work

- Site prep & rough grading
- Basement & foundation digs
- Utility trenching & backfill
- Building pads & compaction
- Demolition & haul-off
- Final grade & drainage

## Frequently asked

### How do bids work?
Call, text, or send the bid form. We walk the site, talk through options, and
put scope, spec, mix, and price in writing — before any work starts.

### Do you do excavation without concrete (or concrete without excavation)?
Yes. The trades are offered together or separately — but when a project needs
both, one crew on one schedule is where we save you the most.

### Are you part of a larger company?
Yes. Braddock Concrete is part of the Alpine Fence & Deck family of
companies — a Spravek company — twenty years of construction craft on the
Wasatch Front, under one accountability line.
